claim: Every set of n distinct points in the Euclidean plane determines at least c*n/sqrt(log n) distinct distances for an absolute constant c>0 (Erdos distinct distances conjecture, erdosproblems.com/89). The best proved lower bound is Guth-Katz 2015 at n/log n; the sqrt(n) x sqrt(n) integer grid shows n/sqrt(log n) is best possible.
domain: discrete geometry / combinatorial geometry / incidence geometry

facets.entities: finite sets of n distinct points in R^2; the set of Euclidean distance values they determine
facets.mechanism: Elekes-Sharir transform to line incidences in R^3, polynomial partitioning, ruled-surface analysis; the residual log loss comes from the degenerate many-points-on-a-line case
facets.method: polynomial partitioning (Guth-Katz), crossing lemma / Szemeredi-Trotter incidence bounds (Szekely, Solymosi-Toth), circle pigeonhole (Erdos 1946)
facets.outcome: lower bound on the minimum number of distinct distances determined by n planar points; closing the sqrt(log n) gap between n/log n and n/sqrt(log n)
